verdicts.correctedClaim: The engine's Sun longitude carries a seasonal error of the truncated VSOP87 Earth series (engine minus Swiss apparent Sun +1.2" in mid-February to -1.67" in early June 2026, zero near April and December), which the Sun's 0.04"/s motion amplifies to solar-return and Sun-ingress instants between ~28 s EARLY (Feb-Mar) and ~42 s LATE (May-Jul); the committed Sun ingresses have signed mean +0.5 s, median |Δ| 9.8 s, max +38.6 s, and the 12-birth return corpus has three negative cases (-15.4, -13.5, -6.4 s). The 37-39 s lag is the mid-year extreme, not a uniform bias; Swiss stays within ~1.2 s of Horizons year-round. Chart-angle impact 0.09-0.24° applies at the extremes.
verdicts.evidence: s5a/s5b rerun identical (solar same-target engine-Swiss median +28.1 s, max +40.0 s, flag 258); cached Horizons arbiter reparsed identical (C9 +38.8 s, C6 +37.4 s, Sun 60° ingress +37.4 s, Swiss -1.2 s in each). My monthly probe (v1b-swiss-compare.py) of engine Sun minus Swiss apparent Sun on the 1st/15th of every 2026 month: +0.324" (Jan 1), +1.199" (Feb 15, event shift -28.5 s), +0.254" (Apr 1), -0.827" (May 1, +20.5 s), -1.672" (Jun 1, +41.9 s), -1.524" (Jul 1, +38.4 s), -1.410" (Oct 15, +34.1 s), +0.010" (Dec 1). Both Horizons solar-return cases (C6, C9) were July births, the worst quadrant; the s9 ingress table shows Pisces -28.9 s and Gemini/Cancer +38.6/+38.0 s with signed mean +0.47 s. The methodology sentence 'accurate to the same standard as every other chart here' is at src/pages/methodology/index.astro:166-167 as cited. Delta-T contribution (-6.5 s) confirmed, so the underlying series error in June is ~1.9".

My run: astronomy-engine MakeTime tt-ut = 71.578 s (2020-01-01), 75.356 s (2026-07-01), 75.497 s (2026-09-22), 76.298 s (2028-01-01); Swiss swe.deltat = 69.361 / 68.843 / 68.821 / 68.8 s; exact TT-UTC since 2017 = 32.184 + 37 = 69.184 s, so the engine clock is 6.2 s fast today. s5b rerun identical: lunar returns same-target engine-Swiss all 12 negative, median -5.25 s, max -6.75 s (Swiss Moon at the engine instant is 1.9-3.9" short of target). s9 rerun: 481 Moon ingresses signed mean -5.87 s, max 10.09 s. Lunar return C1 recomputed from the cached Horizons 1-minute Moon table (target 168.003078°): Horizons 2026-09-11T02:42:01.117Z, engine -6.6 s, Swiss -0.1 s. docs/engine-validation/README.md:81 concedes only the 2100 extrapolation gap (109.5 s); no present-day figure or leap-second table anywhere (grep 69.184/leap second: none). One sub-attribution is wrong in sign but does not affect the claim: omitting the Moon's -0.67" light-time puts the engine Moon AHEAD of the apparent Moon and makes Moon events ~1.2 s earlier (compounding, not offsetting); the smaller-than-6.5 s observed bias is instead offset by the engine's own Moon series residual.

verdicts.correctedClaim: The site (src/lib/engine/longitude-crossings.ts) and @zodiacs/engine ship two crossing solvers with different, but each documented, contracts: the package includes an exact root at `from`, drops an exact-zero sample not confirmed by a later sign change, and throws RangeError above 10,000 samples (all stated in dist/index.d.ts:21-27); the site excludes the lower endpoint, emits exact samples immediately and has no budget (stated by longitude-crossings.test.ts:19-31). No sign-change crossing differs between them; the only practically reachable divergence is that SDK users cannot run scans the site performs (e.g. Moon at the 0.25-day step beyond ~6.8 years, or transit-scan-core's Moon path). docs/engine-validation/README.md:23 ('the site runs the same package') is true for positions (full.ts takes them from @zodiacs/engine/internal) and imprecise only about the solver.
verdicts.evidence: s2 rerun byte-identical: package Sun exact-at-from returns ['2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z'], site returns []; package throws 'Crossing search exceeds the 10,000-sample budget.' for Moon 0° at 0.25 d over 2100/2400/2600 days and Saturn 1900-2100 at 5 d; site Moon 2600 d returns 95 crossings. Code confirmed at dist/index.js:44-112 (MAX_CROSSING_SAMPLES, pendingExact) and longitude-crossings.ts:23-70. But the package's index.d.ts:21-27 documents the budget, the boundary-root inclusion and the tangency drop as its contract, so these are designed semantics, not defects; s3 shows identical pass counts in both copies for all nine real Saturn cases; grep of src/ finds no import of saturnReturn or findLongitudeCrossings from '@zodiacs/engine' (site imports natalChart/ENGINE_VERSION only). No wrong answer is produced by either copy, so the rules' 'major' is not met; it is a real consistency/documentation defect.

verdicts.correctedClaim: transit-window-core.ts:265 applies declared budgets of 0.10°/0.15°/0.20° (documented in docs/engine-validation/transit-windows/README.md:46-48 as moving 0.05° plus natal 0.05°/0.10°/0.15°); on ten real charts over 2026-2027 they label 88/641 windows (13.7%) membership-uncertain and 21 (3.3%) exact-uncertain, while a 0.003° budget labels none and the exact pass count (550) is unchanged at every budget. This is a conservative, documented calibration choice — the labels are honest hedges, not wrong answers — and the tree's own JPL comparison (methodology page: p95 12.1", max 18.6") puts the 0.05° model term at ~10x p95 rather than the 25-100x the finding derives from engine-vs-Swiss residuals. Re-deriving per-body budgets under a new contract version (RESULTS.md:75-83 forbids shrinking the tolerance retroactively) would improve decisiveness; it is not an accuracy gap below Swiss.
verdicts.evidence: s6 rerun byte-identical (641 windows; production budgets 88 membership-uncertain, 21 exact-uncertain, 21 peak.kind 'uncertain'; 0.01° -> 6/2; 0.003° and 0.001° -> 0/0; exactPassesTotal 550 in every run; 12.4 s). transit-window-core.ts:257 accepts angularBudgetDegrees <= 0.2 and :265 sets the defaults as cited. RESULTS.md:10-12 confirms the Uranus D contract is failed-incomplete because its 0.044188° witness sits under the 0.05° budget, and :75-83 states the policy against post-hoc tolerance shrinking. transit-windows README:46-48 documents the budget composition. verdicts.correctedClaim: Outer-planet station instants in sky.json are 20-45 minutes off the DE441 reference and published to the millisecond: the Neptune direct station 2027-12-15 is 09:42:46.8Z in sky.json vs Horizons 09:06:03Z (body 899) / 09:07:36Z (Neptune barycenter 8), +2204/+2110 s, where Swiss is +17/-76 s; the cause is the engine's Neptune series (engine minus Swiss ~+11.1" with a ~0.02-0.05"/day speed error, worth ~36 min at the 5.65e-4 °/day² station acceleration), not the ±6 h finite-difference/16-bisection method, which lands within 6 s of a golden-section extremum on the same longitude. The Pluto comparison must be against the Pluto-Charon barycenter (Horizons 9), which is what Swiss and the engine model: barycenter station 2028-05-09T09:33:32Z, sky.json -2704 s (45 min early), Swiss -241 s; Horizons 999 (body center) is 4052 s earlier because of the 0.08" Charon wobble. The claim that Swiss with the .se1 files is worse than the engine on Pluto is refuted, and the local .se1 files report DE441 (denum 441), not DE431.
verdicts.evidence: s9 rerun identical (92 stations: median 170 s, p95 1396 s, max 2463 s). verdicts.correctedClaim: scripts/build-eclipses.mjs:66-104 stores only type, kind, peak, sign/lon/degree, obscuration and totalMinutes; peaks agree with Swiss to 13.7 s (24/24 kinds match), but none of the contact times, penumbral/partial semi-durations, greatest-eclipse coordinates or local circumstances that astronomy-engine already exposes (sd_penum/sd_partial, GlobalSolarEclipseInfo.latitude/longitude, SearchLocalSolarEclipse) are used, and Saros, magnitudes and observer circumstances that pyswisseph's sol_eclipse_when_glob/where/how/when_loc and lun_eclipse_how/when_loc return are absent. notes: Method: copied the auditor's scripts, lib/ shims and cached Horizons tables to <audit>/verify/production-event-search/ and re-ran s2, s3, s3b, s6, s5a/s5b, s8, s9 and horizons/parse.py there (all outputs byte-identical to the auditor's, elapsed fields aside; Swiss flag 258 asserted throughout); verified lib/ copies equal src/lib/engine/*.ts except import specifiers; wrote v1-engine-epochs.mjs + v1b-swiss-compare.py (Delta-T, monthly engine-vs-Swiss Sun for 2026, Neptune offset/slope, golden-section station on build-sky's own lonAt, aberration mechanism at the 2027-01-07 new moon), v2-eclipse-sd.mjs (raw sd_total, unused eclipse API), and two Horizons requests (COMMAND 9 Pluto Barycenter and 8 Neptune Barycenter, DE441, hourly, QUANTITIES 31; queries and responses cached under verify/.../horizons/). Worktree untouched. Cross-cutting corrections: (1) the Sun timing error is seasonal (-28 s Feb to +42 s Jun), so the summary's '37-39 s late' describes the mid-year extreme only; (2) the auditor's Pluto arbitration used Horizons 999 (body center) while Swiss and the engine model the Pluto-Charon barycenter — against Horizons 9 Swiss is 4 min off and sky.json 45 min, so the 'engine beats Swiss-as-installed on Pluto' exceed-path claim in the summary and swissGap should be dropped; the local .se1 files are DE441-derived (denum 441), not DE431; (3) the package solver's budget and endpoint semantics are documented in its d.ts, and no sign-change crossing differs between the two copies, so finding 5 is a documentation/consistency issue (minor); (4) the transit-window budgets are a documented declared allowance and change no pass count, so finding 6 is a calibration choice (minor); (5) the totality-minutes excess is astronomy-engine's shadow model, not rounding; (6) finding 3's light-time 'offset' sub-attribution has the wrong sign (omitting light-time compounds the early bias) without affecting the claim. Horizons ObsEcLon confirmed as IAU76/80 ecliptic-of-date apparent in UT, matching the Swiss/engine convention for these comparisons.
